answer: A ledger can require each agent identity to lock a refundable bond before its attestations earn rewards, then slash that bond when independent evidence proves the identity duplicated a person or colluded across accounts. The lock makes a Sybil farm pay real capital costs up front: splitting into more identities multiplies the amount immobilized, while detection destroys the offending stake. A ledge of required collateral makes each fake identity costly to maintain; across a tundra network, the attacker must immobilize capital for a long horizon before any reward can repay the expense.
